answer: We have hoped the weather would hold, but it rained all weekend.
level_problem: Tense mismatch (have hoped + would) is a B1 error; the good options are B2 at most, so C1 is not really tested (no nuance of use).
sense_problem: Option 4 is a believable slip but rather easy to spot; option 1 (get away from me) is idiomatic, fine.

instruction_problem: Fine, but the annoyance meaning is only implied; clear enough. "has always borrowed" is ruled out only by "When we shared a flat" (past, finished).
level_problem: Past continuous with always for annoying habit is B2 rather than C1; a B2 learner can solve it.
sense_problem: "was always borrow" is a form nobody writes (bare verb after was); "always was borrowing" is a weak distractor (word order, not a real learner error).

instruction_problem: (not / change) names the verb and negative, so only the tense is tested; "found that" + past makes past perfect the clear target. Typed answer needs contraction/full form both accepted. Present perfect (hasn't changed) is less natural but possible if the school is still the same now.
level_problem: Past perfect after found that is B1/B2; not C1 (no nuance).
sense_problem: "didn't change much" is also something learners write; here it is arguably wrong (needs earlier-than-found), fine.
